title: Map an Unfamiliar Codebase
objective: Given a codebase you didn't write, produce a short written map of its structure, entry points, and one module's responsibilities, using search tools rather than asking the author.
whyThisMatters: Junior engineers spend far more time reading existing code than writing new code from a blank file. Being able to orient yourself in an unfamiliar codebase using command-line search, not tribal knowledge, is a core professional skill.
evidence: The written map (Markdown file) committed to a notes repository
A terminal transcript showing at least 5 of the actual search commands run, with enough surrounding output to see what they found
AI disclosure entry if AI was used to help interpret any part of the code
acceptanceCriteria: The written map names the codebase's entry point and how it was located.
The map lists at least 5 top-level modules or directories with a one-line description of each, based on reading the code, not the README alone.
One module is described in depth: its public functions or classes, and at least one caller and one dependency, each named specifically.
The map states which search commands were used to find each piece of information, for example grep -rn or git log --follow.
